CITY COUNCIL Agenda
Tuesday, August 18, 2026 at 6:00 PM

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA PUBLIC NOTICE is hereby given that the City Council of Spanish Fork, Utah, will hold a public meeting on August 18, 2026 in the Council Chambers, located on the second floor of Library Hall, 80 South Main Street.

-A Work Session Meeting will begin at 4:30 pm in the Explorer Room.

-City Council Meeting will begin at 6:00 pm in the Council Chambers.

Notice is hereby given that:

-In the event of an absence of a quorum, agenda items will be continued to the next regularly scheduled meeting.

-By motion of the Spanish Fork City Council, pursuant to Title 52, Chapter 4 of the Utah Code, the City Council may vote to hold a closed meeting for any of the purposes identified in that Chapter.

- Electronic Participation: Members of the City Council and City Staff may participate by phone, zoom, or other electronic means.


1. WORK SESSION AT 4:30 PM
No formal actions are taken in a work session.


1.1 Financing options and possible timelines for station 61 and public works building

1.2 TUF update and timeline for possible implementation
 
2. CALL TO ORDER

2.1 Prayer & Motivational Message

2.2 Pledge, led by invitation
 
3. PUBLIC COMMENTS
In order to be considerate of everyone attending the meeting and to more closely follow the published agenda times, public comment will be limited to three minutes per person - A spokesperson who has been asked by a group to summarize their concerns will be allowed five minutes to speak - Comments which cannot be made within these limits should be submitted in writing. The Mayor or Council may restrict the comments beyond these guidelines.

4. COUNCIL COMMENTS
 
5. STAFF REPORTS
 
6. CONSENT ITEMS
These items are considered by the City Council to be routine and will be enacted by a single motion. If discussion is desired on any particular consent item, that item may be removed from the consent agenda and considered separately.


6.1 Draft Minutes of City Council for 08-04-2026
08 DRAFT City Council Minutes 08-04-2026 (4).pdf

6.2 Utah County Tourism Tax Advisory Board (TTAB) Grant Agreement
The Airport Manager applied for grant funding through the Utah County Tourism Tax Advisory Board (TTAB) to support the 2026 Wings & Wheels Airshow. Following a successful presentation to the TTAB, the Airport was awarded $25,000 to assist with eligible event expenses, including advertising, event management, and crowd control. Approval is requested to authorize the Mayor, City Recorder, and City Attorney to execute the grant agreement on behalf of Spanish Fork City.

487_2026_AGREEMENTS_6152026.pdfPublic attachment

6.3 FAA Federal Contract Tower Reimbursable Agreement
The FAA has presented Spanish Fork Airport with a Reimbursable Agreement to initiate the Federal Contract Tower Siting Study. While the study is fully reimbursable by the FAA, the Airport is required to advance the approximately $100,000 cost, with reimbursement occurring at a later date.

Execution of this agreement represents the official start of the Federal Contract Tower Program at Spanish Fork Airport and marks a significant milestone in the partnership between the Airport and the FAA. The siting study will identify the optimal location for the future control tower and is the first major step in the design and implementation process. Based on current FAA timelines, construction of the control tower is anticipated to begin within approximately five years of executing this agreement.

The Spanish Fork Airport Advisory Board unanimously recommended approval of the Reimbursable Agreement at its recent meeting. If approved by the City Council, the Airport Manager will be authorized to execute the agreement and return it to the FAA, allowing the siting study to commence.

Reimbursable Agreement AJW-FN-WSA-25-NM-007374 (Reimbursable Agreement).pdfPublic attachment

6.4 HOA West, LLC - Vista View - Fiber Service Agreement
This agreement gives Vista View residents a volume discounted price on SFCN internet.

This Bulk Service Agreement outlines an arrangement between HOA West, LLC and Spanish Fork Community Network (SFCN) to provide fiber internet services to the Vista View development. Key terms include:

-        Services: Fiber internet (up to 500 Mbps) for all units, effective September 1, 2026.

-        Responsibilities: Tenants are automatically enrolled without the option to opt-out. The Recipient is responsible for all wiring, maintenance, and testing, which must meet specific construction standards.

-        Billing: Services are billed at $30 per unit, per month, through the city's municipal utility billing system.

-        Contract Term: The agreement runs for an initial 48-month term, with automatic annual renewals thereafter.

-        Termination: After the first 24 months, the agreement can be terminated with 60 days' notice and payment of a fee equal to 75% of the remaining term costs

7. PUBLIC HEARING
 
7.1 Ordinance to amend Title 15 to modify the parking requirements for properties that have detached accessory dwelling units that are smaller than 650 square feet.
A change to Utah Code will take effect on October 1, 2026. Spanish Fork City is required to modify the zoning code to be consistent with the language in Utah Code that applies to properties with detached accessory dwelling units. This proposed Title 15 amendment would bring Spanish Fork City into conformity with State Law.

ordinance.title15detached.8-18-2026.pdfPublic attachment


7.2 Ordinance to amend the Zoning Map to change the zoning of a property from R-R and R-1-12 to C-2 located at approximately 400 North Spanish Fork Parkway.
This proposal involves changing the zoning of approximately 4.8 acres from R-R Rural Residential and R-1-12 Residential to C-2 General Commercial for property located on the southeast corner of 400 North and Spanish Fork Parkway. Approximately 75 feet of the currently zoned R-1-12 area is proposed to be included in the commercial request. The property is currently vacant and in agricultural production. The proposed commercial area is bisected by existing overhead power lines.

report.cc.hollowacrescommercial.8-18-2026.pdfPublic attachment

ORD No. Z_- 2026 Hollow Acres Commercial Zone Change.pdfPublic attachment

7.3 Ordinance to Amend Title 15 to define and create requirements for data centers and facilities that generate their own electricity
This proposal has been put forth by Volition, a company that would like to construct a data center in Spanish Fork. Volition's proposal has been updated to incorporate recommendations made by the Planning Commission. While the Planning Commission recommended that the proposal be modified, the Commission also failed to make a positive recommendation on the proposal. A motion to recommend approval failed to pass with a three to three tie vote.

memo.volition.8-18-2026_6463 (2).pdf


8.NEW BUSINESS
 

 

8.1Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Building Inspection and Plan Review Services
At the request of Mapleton City, the Spanish Fork Building Inspection Division would like to enter into an interlocal agreement with Mapleton City for building inspection and plan review services. This interlocal agreement would provide building inspections and plan review services on an as-needed basis for both Mapleton and Spanish Fork. This interlocal agreement will fulfil the 2024 Senate Bill 185 requirement for us to provide three options for building inspections if the municipality cannot provide an inspector within three business days. Spanish Fork City doesn't anticipate using this service at the current time.

memo.inspection.interlocal.8.12.2026.pdfPublic attachment

inspection.interlocal.8.12.2026.pdfPublic attachment


9.ADJOURN TO CLOSED MEETING IF NEEDED IN THE EXPLORER ROOM
The Spanish Fork City Council may temporarily recess the regular meeting and convene in a closed session to discuss (a) discussion of the character, professional competence, or physical or mental health of an individual (b) strategy sessions to discuss collective bargaining, (c) strategy sessions to discuss pending or reasonably imminent litigation, (d) strategy sessions to discuss the purchase, exchange, or lease of real property, including any form of a water right or water shares, or to discuss a proposed development agreement, project proposal, or financing proposal related to the development of land owned by the state, (e) strategy sessions to discuss the sale of real property, including any form of a water right or water shares, (f) discussion regarding deployment of security personnel, devices, or systems, (g) investigative proceedings regarding allegations of criminal misconduct as provided in Utah Code § 52-4-205.

 

10.CLOSED MEETING
 
11.ADJOURNMENT

CITY COUNCIL Agenda
Tuesday, August 4, 2026 at 6:00 PM

The public is invited to participate in all Spanish Fork City Council Meetings located at 80 South Main Street, Utah 84660. If you need special accommodation to participate in the meeting, please contact the City Manager's Office at 801-804-4530

The Mayor or Council may restrict the comments beyond these guidelines.

 

 

6.

COUNCIL COMMENTS
 

 

7.

STAFF REPORTS
 

 

8.

SPANISH FORK 101
 

 

8.1

lo Landarch Reconnaissance Survey Presentation
The Spanish Fork Reconnaissance Level Survey documented and evaluated 605 primary structures within the area bounded by 300 South to 400 North and 300 West to 300 East, providing the City's first comprehensive inventory of historic resources in the downtown core. The project was completed by Io LandArch with funding provided through a Certified Local Government (CLG) grant, with 50% funded by the Utah State Historic Preservation Office and 50% funded by Spanish Fork City, for a total project cost of $29,965, of which the City's share was $14,982.50.

The survey serves as a planning tool to help guide future preservation efforts, land-use decisions, and potential historic district considerations, while creating no new regulations or restrictions on property owners. Of the 605 buildings evaluated, 275 (45%) were identified as eligible or contributing historic resources, 263 (43%) were determined to be non-contributing, and 67 (11%) were classified as out-of-period, providing the City with valuable information to preserve and celebrate Spanish Fork's historic character while planning for its future.  SpanishFork_Spreadsheet.pdfPublic attachment APPROVED_Spanish Fork RLS SHPO.pdfPublic attachment FINAL Spanish Fork RLS Report.docxPublic attachment A-1 (Aerial) Survey Extent_6000.pdfPublic attachment A-2 (ALL) PERIODS_SIGNIFICANCE_6000.pdfPublic attachment Spanish Fork Data Analysis (1).pdfPublic attachment

 

 

 

9.

CONSENT ITEMS
These items are considered by the City Council to be routine and will be enacted by a single motion. If discussion is desired on any particular consent item, that item may be removed from the consent agenda and considered separately.

 

 

9.1

Draft City Council Meeting Minutes 07-07-2026
These minutes are from a previous City Council meeting and need to be approved.

07 DRAFT City Council Minutes 07-07-2026 (5).pdfPublic attachment

 

 

 

9.2

BizSolar Program Interconnection Agreement
The BizSolar Interconnection  agreement between Spanish Fork City and Wheeler Cat in order to connect their onsite solar generation to Spanish Fork's power system. 

 

 

 

9.3

General Aviation Impact Fee Exception Request
General Aviation Development, LLC has requested a special exception to the water and sewer impact fees for the proposed airport hangar development at the Spanish Fork Airport.

CC Memo - General Aviation Impact Fee Request.pdfPublic attachment 7-13-26 Water Impact Fee Reduction Request General Aviation Development-1.pdfPublic attachment

 

 

 

9.4

Franchise Agreement for Strata Networks
This agreement is a new franchise agreement with Spanish Fork City for Strata Networks. It is a standard agreement based upon the provisions of the Municipal Telecommunications License Tax Act, Utah Code Ann. § 10-1-401 et seq., and Spanish Fork's Telecommunications Rights-of-Way ordinance found in Title 5, Chapter 32, of the Spanish Fork Municipal Code.

The agreement grants the right to locate wires, cables, and other telecommunications facilities within the public rights-of-way in return for payment of the municipal telecommunications license tax. It addresses relocation of facilities, construction standards, indemnification, insurance, and other typical provisions.

Because the City's ordinance, state, and federal law require approval of franchise agreements on a competitively neutral basis, this item, as have other franchise agreements in the past, is placed on the Consent Agenda.

Franchise Agreement_Spanish Fork City_Strata Networks (Partially Executed).pdfPublic attachment

 

 

 

9.5

Direct Award Grant Funds Agreement
 The proposed agreement between the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT) and Spanish Fork City provides a $3,000,000 direct legislative grant for the design and construction of Taxiway Bravo Phase III at the Spanish Fork Airport. The funds will be distributed in four quarterly payments of $750,000 during Fiscal Year 2026-2027 and must be used solely for the approved project, with all funds expended by December 31, 2029. The agreement requires the City to maintain detailed financial records, submit annual and final reports, and demonstrate project progress and performance, including improvements to airport safety and efficiency such as reducing runway crossings and taxiway congestion.

Spanish Fork Grant Agreement.docx (3).pdfPublic attachment

 

 

 

10.

NEW BUSINESS
 

 

10.1

Ordinance to Create Provisional Business Licenses
 If adopted, this ordinance would modify Title 5 of the Municipal Code to create provisions for the administration of Provisional Business Licenses.

memo.title5provisional.8-4-2026.pdfPublic attachment

 

 

 

10.2

Personnel Policy - Definitions Update
Staff is recommending this policy update to better align the City's Affordable Care Act (ACA) compliance practices with operational needs. The ACA permits employers to use a measurement period of up to twelve months to determine full-time eligibility for health insurance.

Moving to a twelve-month measurement period will provide greater flexibility in scheduling part-time employees and those working seasonally while ensuring they remain within annual ACA eligibility limits.

Resolution - Personnel Policy - August 4, 2026.docx.pdfPublic attachment The change will also simplify administration by consolidating multiple non-benefited employee classifications into a single part-time classification, making the policy easier to administer and helping the City more effectively maintain compliance with the Affordable Care Act.

 

 

 

10.3

Board and Commission Appointments
Appointing two Planning Commission Members and Reappointing a Airport Board Member

 

11.

DISCUSSION - No action will be taken on this item at this time. If the City Council would like to consider taking action on this matter in the future, the item may be placed on a future agenda for discussion and possible action.
Large Power Users, Islanded Power, and Data Centers

13.

CLOSED MEETING
 

 

14.

ADJOURNMENT
 

City Council

 

The City Council usually meets on the first and third Tuesdays of every month (except only one meeting in July and December: July 7, 2026 and December 8, 2026) at 6 pm preceded by a work session at the City Offices located at 80 South Main Street. Please check each agenda for times and dates. If you need help call 801-804-4530.

 

Mayor Mike Mendenhall, Council member Stacy Beck, Council member Shane Marshall, Council member Kevin Oyler, and Council member Jesse Cardon and Council member Landon Tooke, are honored to serve you in the capacity of Mayor and City Council members. To send an email to the entire council, address your email to council@spanishfork.org. This will automatically send an email to each council member.

 

We strive to make wise decisions to continue the fine traditions made by those who have gone before us. These people built a solid foundation upon which our community stands - the foundation is based upon principles of hard work, dedication and sacrifice. Our meetings are open to the public and we hope to hear from you so we can work together to continue to build our community on sound principles.

notices.agenda_text:
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND BONDS TO BE ISSUED

PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN pursuant to the provisions of the Local Building Authority Act, Title 17D, Chapter 2, Utah Code Annotated 1953, as amended, the Local Government Bonding Act, Title 11, Chapter 14, Utah Code, as amended and the Utah Refunding Bond Act, Title 11, Chapter 27, Utah Code Annotated 1953, as amended (collectively, the 'Act'), that on June 2, 2026, the Governing Board (the 'Governing Board') of the Local Building Authority of Spanish Fork City, Utah (the 'Authority') adopted a resolution (the 'Resolution') declaring its intention to issue its Lease Revenue and Refunding Bonds, Series 2026 (the 'Bonds'), and calling a public hearing to receive input from the public with respect to the issuance of the Bonds.

TIME, PLACE AND LOCATION OF PUBLIC HEARING

The Authority shall hold a public hearing on July 7, 2026, at the hour of 6:00 p.m. The location of the public hearing is at the City offices of Spanish Fork, Utah (the 'City') located at 40 South Main Street, Spanish Fork, Utah. The purpose of the hearing is to receive input from the public with respect to: (a) the proposed Bonds, and (b) any potential economic impact that the improvements, facility or property financed in whole or in part with the proceeds of the Bonds may have on the private sector. All members of the public are invited to attend and participate.

PURPOSE FOR ISSUING BONDS

The Authority intends to issue the Bonds to provide funds to (a) finance costs of the construction of a fire station and public works building and all related improvements (the 'Series 2026 Project'); (b) refund certain outstanding bonds of the Authority; (c) fund any required deposits to a debt service reserve fund; and (d) pay costs associated with the issuance of the Bonds.

PARAMETERS OF THE BONDS

The Authority intends to issue the Bonds in a principal amount of not to exceed Eighty-Three Million Dollars ($83,000,000), to bear interest at a rate or rates of not to exceed six percent (6.00%) per annum, to mature in not more than twenty-one (21) years from their date or dates, and to be sold at a price not less than ninety-eight percent (98%) of the total principal amount thereof, plus accrued interest, if any, to the date of delivery of the Bonds.

The Bonds are to be issued and sold by the Authority pursuant to the Resolution, including as attachments to said Resolution a form of a General Indenture of Trust and Third Supplemental Indenture of Trust (collectively, the 'Indenture') and a form of a Master Lease Agreement and Second Amendment to Master Lease Agreement (together, the 'Lease'), which were before the Governing Board at the time of the adoption of the Resolution. The Indenture and the Lease are to be executed by the Authority and/or the City with such terms and provisions and any changes thereto as authorized by the Resolution.

SECURITY FOR THE BONDS

4916-0246-9554, v. 1
The Bonds are payable solely from the rents, revenues and other income received by the Authority from the leasing of the Series 2026 Project to the City on an annually renewable basis (the 'Lease Revenues') and any other monies available under the Indenture.

OUTSTANDING BONDS SECURED BY LEASE REVENUES

The Authority currently has $26,101,000 bonds outstanding secured by Lease Revenues of which $10,536,000 are anticipated to be refunded with a portion of the proposed Series 2026 Bonds, together with $70,000,000 from the proposed Series 2026 Bonds for new projects, for an estimated total outstanding par of $91,860,000 once the Series 2026 Bonds are issued and the refunding completed.

OTHER OUTSTANDING BONDS OF THE AUTHORITY

Information regarding all of the Authority's outstanding bonds may be found in the City's audited financial report (the 'Financial Report') at https://reporting.auditor.utah.gov/searchreports/s/. For additional information, including any more recent than as of the date of the Financial Report please contact Seth Perrins, City Manager at (801) 804-4531.

TOTAL ESTIMATED COST

Based on an estimate of the current interest rate and financing plan, the estimated total debt service cost of the Bonds, if held until maturity, is $96,202,094.
A copy of the Resolution and the forms of Indenture and the Lease are on file in the City offices, located at 40 South Main Street, Spanish Fork, Utah, where they may be examined during regular business hours from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, for a period of at least thirty (30) days from and after the last date of posting of this notice.
NOTICE IS FURTHER GIVEN that a period of thirty (30) days from and after the date of the posting of this notice is provided by law during which (i) any person in interest shall have the right to contest the legality of the Resolution, the Indenture, the Lease, or the Bonds, or any provision made for the security and payment of the Bonds, and after such time, no one shall have any cause of action to contest the regularity, formality or legality thereof for any cause whatsoever, and (ii) active voters (as defined in Section 20A-1-102 of the Utah Code) within the City may sign a written petition requesting an election to authorize the issuance of the Bonds. If written petitions which have been signed by at least twenty percent (20%) of the active voters of the City are filed with the Authority during said 30-day period, the Authority shall be required to hold an election to obtain voter authorization prior to the issuance of the Bonds. If fewer than twenty percent (20%) of the active voters of the City file a written petition during said 30-day period, the Authority may proceed to issue the Bonds without an election.

DATED this June 3, 2026.

NOTICE OF INTENT TO ISSUE A LEASE REVENUE BOND AND PUBLIC HEARING

PUBLIC NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN pursuant to the provisions of the Local Building Authority Act, Title 17D, Chapter 2, Utah Code Annotated 1953, as amended, the Local Government Bonding Act, Title 11, Chapter 14, Utah Code, as amended, and the Utah Refunding Bond Act, Title 11, Chapter 27, Utah Code Annotated 1953, as amended (collectively, the 'Act'), that the Governing Board (the 'Governing Board') of the Local Building Authority of Spanish Fork City, Utah (the 'Authority') intends to issue its Lease Revenue and Refunding Bonds, Series 2026 (the 'Series 2026 Bonds') and will hold a public hearing to provide members of the public desiring to be heard an opportunity to present testimony on the proposed issuance of the Series 2026 Bonds in accordance with Sections 11-14-103 and 17D-2-501 of the Utah Code Annotated 1953, as amended. Said public hearing will be held on July 7, 2026, at 6:00 p.m., at 40 South Main Street, Spanish Fork, Utah. The purpose of the Series 2026 Bonds is to provide funds to (a) finance the costs of construction of a fire station and public works building and all related improvements (the 'Series 2026 Project'); (b) refund certain outstanding bonds of the Authority; (c) fund any required debt service reserve fund; and (d) pay costs associated with the issuance of the Series 2026 Bonds. The length of term of the Series 2026 Bonds shall not exceed 21 years. The average annual amount that the Authority will be required to pay in principal and interest on the Series 2026 Bonds is $5,655,595. The intended lessee of the facility to be constructed using proceeds from the Series 2026 Bonds is Spanish Fork City, Utah (the 'City') and the expected annual amount of lease payments that the City will pay is $5,684,834. The Authority anticipates taking action on the proposal to issue the Series 2026 Bonds directly following the public hearing at the same meeting listed above.

DATED this June 3, 2026.

/s/ Tara Silver
Secretary-Treasurer

NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDING CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS

SPANISH FORK CITY

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Spanish Fork City Council will hold a public hearing and consider adoption of an ordinance amending the City's Construction Standards during its regular meeting on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. at Spanish Fork City Hall, 80 South Main Street, Spanish Fork, Utah.

The proposed amendments to the Construction Standards include the following:

- Addition of a section for boring inspections and testing.
- Modifications to communication plan requirements for excavation permits.
- Modifications to 5-foot sewer manhole requirements.
- Addition of a section establishing the minimum depth of sewer mains.
- Clarification that inlets are not permitted within driveway access areas.
- Modifications to electrical standards.
- Modifications to water standard drawings.
- Modifications to mow strip, curb wall, and tree planting standard drawings.
- Addition of 2-inch and 3-inch PI Filter standard drawings.
- Modifications to Power & Light standard drawings.

The purpose of these amendments is to update and clarify engineering, utility, construction, and infrastructure standards applicable to public improvements and development within Spanish Fork City.

Interested persons are invited to attend the public hearing and provide comments regarding the proposed ordinance. Copies of the proposed amendments are available for public inspection at the Spanish Fork City Engineering Department during regular business hours or call 801-804-4543.

Published this 2 day of June, 2026.

Spanish Fork City

City Recorder

notices.title: Spanish Fork City Council Notice to Spanish Fork City Utility Customers 2027
notices.agenda_text:
NOTICE TO SPANISH FORK CITY UTILITY CUSTOMERS

State law requires that the City provide an annual disclosure on funds transferred from a utility enterprise fund to any other fund. The City has budgeted the following transfers. 

The City of Spanish Fork has budgeted for the transfer from each utility fund to the general fund as a dividend to Spanish Fork taxpayers. This dividend is the result of the rate payers' investment in the City's utility infrastructure. These funds are used each year to help cover costs of important city services like police, fire, library, senior center, parks and recreation, and other city functions. The utility transfer helps keep property taxes low in Spanish Fork. If City utility services were provided by private utility vendors, these dividends would instead be paid to the private investor-owners. Because Spanish Fork residents are the investor-owners, these dividends are used to offset what otherwise would be a significant increase in property tax rates. These transfers are of funds which cannot be defined as a reasonable allocation of costs between funds. These amounts will not be repaid. 

The amounts of the transfers are as follows:	Dollar Amount          	% of Expenditures 
From the Power Fund to the General Fund	$ 1,310,000	  3.3 % From the Water Fund to the General Fund 	$ 352,000		2.6 % 
From the Sewer Fund to the General Fund	$ 152,000	0.9 %
From the Solid Waste Fund to the General Fund 	$ 50,000 	 1.3 % 
From the Broadband Fund to the General Fund 	$ 633,171 	  5.7 % 

Spanish Fork City also has a debt obligation that the Power Fund is helping make payments on. The funds are to pay for the Justice Center (Police/Court Building). This transfer is for funds which cannot be defined as a reasonable allocation of costs between funds. These amounts will not be repaid. 

The amount of this transfer is as follows:        	Dollar Amount	 % of Expenditures 
From the Power Fund to the Debt Service Fund 	$ 679,503 	1.7 %

A public hearing will be held on Tuesday, June 2, 2026 at 6 p.m. at the City Council Chambers, located at 80 South Main Street, Spanish Fork, Utah. The public hearing will be to discuss the proposed dividend transfers in the Fiscal Year 2027 Budget. The fiscal year begins July 1, 2026 and ends June 30, 2027. 

Thank you for your support and involvement as a utility customer of Spanish Fork.
